title: Mushroom & Rice Burger
description: If you have any leftover rice, this recipe is a great way to use it up. We also love batch-making this recipe! We enjoy a couple of burger patties the night they're made, and we freeze the rest. It makes for a speedy dinner when you're short on time.
ingredients: 1 Tbsp (15ml) vegetable oil, plus extra for frying
4.9 oz (140g) button mushrooms, minced cremini mushrooms
⅓ cups (29g) raw walnuts, minced raw almonds
1½ cups (270g) cooked brown lentils cooked black beans cooked pinto beans
1 cup (195g) cooked brown rice cooked white rice
1 cup (20g) arugula any lettuce of choice
instructions: Add the ground flaxseeds and water to a large bowl, mix, and set aside.
Add the oil to a sauté pan on high heat. When hot, add the onions and garlic and sauté until lightly golden, about 5 minutes.
Then add the mushroom and walnuts, and cook until most of the moisture has evaporated, which takes about 5 - 8 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, cumin, and coriander and continue to cook until all the moisture is evaporated. Remove the pan from the heat.
Add the lentils to the same bowl as the flaxseeds and mash as best you can using an immersion blender, potato masher, or fork.
Transfer the cooked mushroom mixture to the bowl, along with the remaining patty ingredients. Using your hands, mix well and then form into burger patties.
Heat up a bit of oil in a large pan on medium heat. Cook the patties until golden on each side, about 2 - 3 minutes per side.
When the patties are ready, assemble your burger, and enjoy!
Keep the patties in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Store well sealed in the freezer separated by pieces of parchment paper for up to 1 month.

title: Thai Sweet Potato & Chickpea Green Curry
description: Whip up this creamy Thai Green Curry with chickpeas and sweet potatoes in under 10 ingredients! A quick, flavourful, and protein-packed recipe perfect for busy nights.
ingredients: 1 cup (200g) uncooked white rice, rinsed vegan naans
1 medium sweet potato, peeled, cut into 1 cm cubes medium potato
1¼ cups (205g) cooked chickpeas cooked brown lentils
instructions: Cook the rice according to the package instructions.
Add the oil and onion to a large pot on high heat. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the curry paste, and mash into the garlic and onion mixture until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Then add the sweet potato, coconut milk, chickpeas, and water*.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 10 - 15 minutes, partially covered, until the sweet potatoes are cooked.
Remove from heat and add the spinach, stirring to wilt.
Serve over rice or with naan, and enjoy!
* Taste test after adding the water. Depending on how thick you like your curry, you may want to add more water to thin it out.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Beetroot Quinoa Salad with Orange Ginger Dressing
description: This vibrant quinoa chickpea arugula salad with beets, orange, and a tangy tahini-ginger dressing is a light yet satisfying meal packed with flavour and nourishment.
ingredients: 1½ cups (245g) cooked chickpeas cooked brown lentils
3 cups (60g) arugula fresh spinach any lettuce of choice
1 orange, peeled, sliced into thin rounds fresh strawberries red grapes grapefruit wedges
1 pinch ground black pepper, plus more to taste
instructions: Add the quinoa, water, and bouillon to a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover and cook for 15 minutes. Then remove the heat and keep covered.
Make the dressing by adding all the ingredients to a bowl. Mix well.
Transfer the dressing to to the saucepan with the quinoa, and add the chickpeas as well. Toss to combine.
To serve, start with the arugula as a base, top with quinoa and chickpea mixture, and garnish with the orange slices and roasted beetroots. Enjoy!
Best to assemble and dress the salad before enjoying.
If saving for later, store the dressing separate from the other components of the salad. Keep in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Once assembled, store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a day.

title: Eggplant Pesto Orzo
description: This creamy eggplant pesto orzo is an easy, flavorful dish that’s super simple to make. The tender orzo pasta is paired with sautéed eggplant and vegan red pesto, creating a rich and savoury base. Topped with crunchy toasted croutons (optional, but they add a delightful crunch), this meal strikes the perfect balance between creamy and crispy textures. It’s a comforting, satisfying, and budget-friendly vegan recipe, perfect for a quick weeknight dinner
ingredients: 1 cup (180g) dry orzo pasta dry gluten-free orzo pasta
1 medium eggplant, cut into 1 cm cubes†
¼ cups (60ml) soy cooking cream any unsweetened plant-based milk of choice
instructions: Cook the orzo according to the package instructions.
Meanwhile, add the croutons, oil, and Italian seasoning mix to a small pan on medium heat. Cook for 5 minutes, until golden. Set aside.
Add the oil to a sauté pan. When hot, add the onion and cook for 5 - 7 minutes, until golden. Add splashes of water as needed to deglaze the pan.
Add the tomato paste and pesto and cook for 1 minute.
Add the remaining orzo ingredients. Cook for 8 - 10 minutes, or until the eggplant is softened to your liking.
When the orzo is al dente, drain it, and stir it into the pan. Taste test and add more pesto and cooking cream to taste.
Serve with the seasoned croutons on top. Enjoy!
†For us 1 eggplant was about 290 g.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Reheat with a bit of water, milk, or vegetable stock to make it creamy again.

title: Hummus Pasta Salad
description: Presenting a straightforward yet delightfully tasty pasta salad that comes together effortlessly. The dressing combines the richness of roasted red bell pepper and hummus, enhancing the dish with an added creaminess. It's an ideal choice for a swift lunch or dinner option.
ingredients: 7.1 oz (200g) dry fusilli pasta any dry pasta of choice
1½ roasted red bell pepper from a jar
instructions: Cook the pasta until al dente. When cooked, drain, then add to a large bowl.
Meanwhile, add oil to a medium pan. When hot, add the zucchini and cook until lightly golden, about 4 - 5 minutes.
Then add the curry powder and salt. Cook for 2 - 3 more minutes. Stir often. Then transfer to the large bowl as well.
Add all the dressing ingredients to a small food processor. Blend until smooth.
Add the carrot, tomato, spinach, and parsley (if using) to the large bowl.
Drizzle over the dressing and toss to combine. Enjoy!
†For us, 1 zucchini weighed 320 g.
The assembled salad is best enjoyed immediately.
Store the pasta salad base separately from the sauce in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Combine when ready to enjoy.

title: Vegan Butter 'Chicken' with Baked Tofu
description: This veganized butter chicken is sure to become a new dinner favourite! It's beautifully spiced and wonderfully creamy. The grilled tofu has a great texture, bursting with flavour, while the blended cashews and coconut milk add a velvety creaminess to this delicious curry.
ingredients: 16 oz (450g) firm tofu, pressed, cut into 1 cm cubes tempeh
½ cups (130g) unsweetened soy yogurt any unsweetened plant-based yogurt of choice
1⅔ cups (400ml) canned full-fat coconut milk canned light coconut milk
instructions: Soak the raw cashews in boiling water to soften. Set aside.
Line a baking tray and preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C)*.
Add all the baked tofu ingredients to a large bowl and mix.
Transfer to the baking tray and bake for 15 - 20 minutes, stirring once or twice. Keep an eye on it to prevent burning.
Meanwhile, add the oil, garlic, onion, jalapeño, and ginger to a large pot on high heat. Cook until lightly golden.
Add in the spices and cook for 1 more minute, stirring throughout to toast them.
Then add the remaining curry ingredients, including the drained cashews.
Blend everything using an immersion blender or transfer to a standing blender to blend until smooth. Let simmer on low, and cover with a lid.
Once the tofu is golden, remove it from the oven and add it to the pot. Give it a gentle stir.
Serve with naan or rice. Enjoy!
* We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection).
Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Miso Sesame Soba Noodles
description: Within 20 minutes, you can serve this delicious bowl of noodles on the table. These noodles are easy to make and packed with intense umami and vinegary flavour. This dish is delicious both hot and cold and suitable for any season.
ingredients: 2 Tbsp (30ml) dark soy sauce sodium-reduced soy sauce tamari
instructions: Mix together the dressing ingredients in a jar or bowl*. If the mixture is too thick, add a small splash of water as needed. Set aside.
Cook the soba noodles according to the package instructions ina. saucepan. For us, this took about 5 minutes. Then drain.
Meanwhile, add the oil to a sauté pan on high heat. When hot, add in the mushrooms and edamame beans and cook for 5 minutes.
Then add the soba noodles, and dressing. Let everything heat through.
Divide the noodles between your bowls, and top with sliced avocado, radishes, green onions, and sesame seeds. Enjoy!
†About 14 medium mushrooms
* This recipe has a pronounced vinegar taste. If you'd prefer, add less vinegar.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Speedy Pea & Basil Pesto Pasta
description: If you are looking for a fast, filling, and nutritious dinner idea, you've found it here. The aromatic basil leaves and toasted pine nuts blended together make a delicious pesto that's used to give this pasta a wonderful creaminess.
ingredients: 8.8 oz (250g) dry linguine noodles dry gluten-free pasta
2 roasted red bell peppers from a jar, from a jar, diced red bell peppers sun-dried tomatoes in oil
1½ cups (220g) fresh green peas frozen green peas
instructions: Cook the pasta according to package instruction in salted boiling water until al dente.
Add the oil and garlic to a medium pan on high heat. Cook for 2 minutes, then transfer to a small food processor.
To the now-empty pan, add the oil and shallots. Cook until golden, adding the bell peppers at the end just to heat through.
Meanwhile, returning to the food processor, add in the lemon juice, peas, pine nuts, basil, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Blend until creamy.
When the pasta is al dente, drain, and transfer it back to the empty pot. Add the shallot mixture and pea pesto to the pasta, and toss to combine.
Plate with arugula, garnish, and enjoy!
Store the pasta and pea pesto separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 4 days. Combine when ready to enjoy.

title: Golden Tempeh Nourish Bowl
description: For a filling and nourishing lunch or dinner packed with antioxidants, look no further! The tempeh is crispy and coated in a zesty sauce, and the seasoned red rice pairs so nicely with the sauteed mushrooms and kale.
ingredients: 8.8 oz (250g) tempeh, cut into 1 cm x 2 cm pieces firm tofu
1½ cups (240g) uncooked red rice, soaked overnight† uncooked brown rice uncooked basmati rice
2 tsp (10ml) toasted sesame oil vegetable oil
2 portobello mushrooms, thinly sliced button mushrooms cremini mushrooms
2 carrots, thinly sliced sugar snap peas
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together the orange juice, tahini, garlic, miso, sambal, ginger, and turmeric.
Add the pieces of tempeh to the bowl, toss, and let marinate for as long as possible - either just while preparing the rest of the recipe, or overnight to maximize flavour.
Meanwhile, chop the mushrooms, carrots, and kale. Set aside.
Add the rice, water, and bouillon to a medium pot. Cook partially covered at a gentle simmer for about 20 minutes. When cooked, remove from the heat, fully cover, and let sit for 5 minutes.
Separate the marinated tempeh from the sauce, and place it in a bowl. Reserve the leftover marinade as this will be the dressing for the nourish bowl.
Sprinkle cornstarch over the tempeh and toss to coat.
Preheat the oil in a large pan on medium-high heat. When hot, add the tempeh and panfry until the tempeh is golden on all sides, tossing every few minutes.
To a separate pan, add the sesame oil and mushrooms. Cook for 3 - 4 minutes.
Then add the carrots, kale, salt, and pepper and cook for 3 - 4 more minutes.
To assemble, layer some rice on the bottom of a bowl. Top with the sautéed kale mix and pan-fried tempeh. Add other desired toppings, drizzle the reserved golden tahini sauce on top, and enjoy!
†If unable to soak the rice overnight, cook according to the package instructions as more water will be needed to cook the rice.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Store the sauce separately until you are ready to eat.

title: Grilled Red Pepper Pesto Pasta
description: Simple meals are the best! This delicious roasted red pepper pesto pasta is a perfect weekday dinner idea and comes together with under 10 ingredients. It's packed with veggies and makes a hearty meal for the whole family.
ingredients: 1 orange bell pepper, quartered red bell pepper
½ tsp ground black pepper, divided
14 oz (400g) dry spaghetti noodles dry gluten-free pasta
¼ cups (38g) sun-dried tomatoes in oil, drained
¼ cups (31g) roasted walnuts roasted sunflower seeds
instructions: Add the oil to a large pan on high heat. When hot, add the bell peppers in a single layer. Sprinkle over a bit of salt and pepper. Cook until blistered, then flip to cook on the other side*.
Push the blistered bell peppers to the side of the pan. Add more oil and cook the garlic until lightly golden, about 2 - 3 minutes. Transfer everything to a food processor or blender.

Return the same pan to the heat, and add more oil and zucchini. Sprinkle over salt and pepper, and try not to disturb the zucchini as it cooks. Flip only when golden. Meanwhile, cook the pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water.
Returning to the food processor, add in the sun-dried tomato, and walnuts. Blend until smooth, but some small chunks can remain, if desired.

In the last two minutes of the pasta cooking, add the peas to the cooking water. When the pasta is al dente, drain. Then return the drained pasta to the pot. Add the cooked zucchini and blended red bell pepper mixture to the pot. Toss everything to coat.
One heated through, serve while hot. Garnish if desired, and enjoy!
* To speed up this recipe, skip this step and use roasted bell peppers from a jar.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Creamy Gnocchi Soup
description: This creamy gnocchi soup is wholesome and comforting— perfect for a chilly weekday dinner. It's packed with veggies and enriched with vegan cream for a velvety, smooth broth. Nutritional yeast and miso lend a delicious umami flavour, while a final drizzle of lemon juice brightens and ties all the flavours together.
ingredients: 1 cup (240ml) soy cooking cream any plant-based cooking cream of choice canned full-fat coconut milk
instructions: Add oil to a large pot on medium-high heat. When hot, add the garlic, celery, onion, and carrot. Cook for 3 - 5 minutes, until golden.
Add the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring throughout to toast.
Add the bouillon cubes, water, cream, nutritional yeast, spice mix, and miso. Cook at a gentle simmer, partially covered, for 10 minutes.
When the veggies have cooked to your liking, add the gnocchi, spinach, and green peas. Cook for 3 - 4 minutes, or until the gnocchi and peas are cooked.
Serve in bowls, add some fresh lemon juice, garnish as desired, and enjoy!
†For us, 2 celery ribs weighed 100 g.
†For us, 1 carrot weighed 100 g.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Coconut Thai Green Curry Noodle Soup
description: This curry is a spicy one! Curries can be found all over the world, but green curry originates from central Thailand. In our time travelling through Thailand, we enjoyed curries for breakfast, lunch, and dinner without ever tiring of it. The name 'green' curry comes from the colour of the dish, as green chillies are used to create the curry paste, so it packs quite a bit of heat along with its intense and bold flavours.
ingredients: 13 oz (375g) firm tofu, pressed, cut into 1 cm cubes
1⅔ cups (400ml) canned full-fat coconut milk canned light coconut milk
6.3 oz (180g) dry brown rice noodles quick-cooking ramen noodles dry white rice noodles
1 bell pepper, thinly sliced small broccoli
instructions: Add the oil to a large pan on medium-high heat. When hot, add the tofu and sprinkle with salt. Cook until golden on all sides, about 8 - 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, add the green broth ingredients to a blender. Blend until smooth.
Add the rice noodles to a large bowl and pour boiling water over top to submerge. Drain after 2 minutes once the noodles are al dente* and rinse under warm water. Divide the noodles into your bowls.
Once the tofu is golden and crispy on all sides, transfer to a bowl and set aside.
Return the same pan to heat and add the oil. When hot, add the garlic and shallots and cook until lightly golden, about 3 minutes.
Add the curry paste, lemongrass, kaffir leaves, and ginger. Sauté for a minute.
Add the bell pepper, and cook for an extra 3 minutes.
Add the snow peas and cook for 30 seconds, before transferring the green blended broth to the pan. Turn off the heat once heated through.
Remove the lemongrass and kaffir leaves before serving.
Finally, squeeze in the lime juice, stir, and then ladle the broth over top of the noodles.
Add the tofu to the top of the bowl, and add any desired garnishes. Enjoy!
* Refer to package instructions as you may need to cook your noodles differently.
If batch-making ahead of time, store the cooked noodles and broth separately and combine once heated, otherwise the noodles soak up too much of the broth and become too soft.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
